title: Sandy Beaches in Rijeka, Croatia: Real Sand Nearby 2027
metaDescription: Rijeka has no true sandy beach. Surface guide to its pebble beaches, plus the nearest real sand in Crikvenica, Krk and Rab, with travel times.
content:
## Is there a sandy beach in Rijeka?

No. Rijeka is a port city on a steep, rocky coast, and its swimming spots are pebble beaches, concrete platforms and rock ledges. Anything described as sand within the city limits is a small patch or imported material. The nearest places with sand mixed into the shoreline are in Crikvenica, 40 minutes south. The nearest true sand is on the island of Krk, and the best is Rajska plaža on Rab.

## Beach surfaces in Rijeka, beach by beach

### Kantrida and Ploče (west of the centre)
Kantrida sits opposite the old football stadium, about 6 km from the centre. It is a pebble beach, partly equipped with concrete surfaces. Ploče is a Blue Flag beach in the same district. It lies 250 metres from Kantrida Beach, and there is a large car park near Kantrida from which Ploče is a few minutes' walk. The water deepens gradually at both. That makes them workable for children, but entry is over pebbles and concrete, not soft sand. Shade is limited, and weekends in July and August are busy with locals. Bus 1 from the city centre reaches Kantrida. The area has a section where dogs are allowed.

### Pećine, Glavanovo and Preluk (city side)
These are urban beaches of pebble and concrete. Bus line 1 also serves the Pećine area to the east. They suit a short swim after work or sightseeing. They do not suit anyone who wants a soft seabed.

### Kostrena (east, 8-9 km)
Kostrena is a string of connected coves, not one beach. It is a series of connected pebble beaches stretching for several kilometres along the coast. The surface is the finest in the Rijeka area: a clean, very fine pebble beach. Žurkovo is the exception. It is pebble with a few rocks. Entry is steeper at the rocky coves, so Kostrena works for older children and confident swimmers more than toddlers. Pine shade exists behind several coves. Parking is small and fills by late morning in summer. Arrive before 10:00 or take the local bus.

## Nearest beaches with real sand

### Crikvenica (about 40 minutes)
Crikvenica is the practical answer for families. It is about 40 minutes from Rijeka by car. The city beach is a Blue Flag stretch of sandy and smooth pebble. Expect sand mixed with fine pebble, not a Caribbean-style dune. Water is shallow near the shore, there are many cafés and lifeguards, and the beach is crowded in August. Smaller options nearby are Dramalj, 3 km from Crikvenica, and Poli mora, suitable for small children. Concrete platforms around the piers, in Dramalj and Selce, are for sunbathing, not for kids.

### Krk island (about 1 hour)
Krk is connected to the mainland by bridge, so no ferry is needed. The small sandy beaches are Sv. Marak near Risika, Meline and Čižići in Soline Bay. Sv. Marek in Risika is 130 m long, with parking, showers, toilets, natural shade and a small seasonal bar. Soline Bay's shallow, sheltered water suits toddlers. Parking at all of them is limited in peak season.

### Rab island, Lopar (about 2.5-3 hours)
This is the only place near Rijeka that offers sand in quantity. Rajska plaža has about 1.5 km of fine sand in a very shallow bay. Water stays knee-deep far out, so it is the best choice in the region for small children. Shade is thin on the open sand, so bring an umbrella. At the peak of the season it can be hard to find a sunbathing spot. The quieter option is a smaller Lopar bay, such as Livačina, which has a sandy 300 m shore with facilities. The bays furthest from the car parks stay quiet even in August, because they take a twenty-minute walk through pines. Pudarica near Rab town is a mix of sand and fine pebbles.

**How to get there:** The Jadrolinija ferry from Valbiska on Krk to Lopar takes about 80 minutes. Valbiska is roughly 50 minutes' drive from Rijeka, so allow a full day. A Jadrolinija catamaran also links Rijeka, Rab and Novalja for foot passengers. That option is better for car-free travellers. Check the summer timetable before booking.

### Susak island
Susak is made of fine sand rather than rock. Its main beach, Bok, is a wide shallow bay. The island has no cars. Reach it by ferry from Mali Lošinj; check whether a sailing from Rijeka runs on your date. It works as a long day trip, not a quick beach stop.

## Local tips on sand and pebbles

- Pack water shoes for every Rijeka and Kostrena beach. They matter more here than sunscreen.
- Choose Crikvenica over Kantrida for toddlers. The gentle entry and sandy sections matter more than the shorter drive.
- Go to Rab on a weekday and before 10:00. The Paradise Beach car park and sand fill up in July and August.
- Visit in June or September. Water is warm enough and the beaches are far less crowded.

## Verdict: does Rijeka suit people who want sand?

Not as a beach base. Rijeka is a better city than a beach destination, and its pebbles and concrete will disappoint anyone set on sand. The sensible plan is to stay in Rijeka or Kostrena for the city and use Crikvenica as a 40-minute sand-and-fine-pebble day trip. If real sand is the goal, base yourself on Krk or Rab instead. Rijeka works for pebble-tolerant travellers, not for sand seekers.

faq.question: Does Rijeka have a sandy beach?
faq.answer: No. Rijeka's beaches at Kantrida, Ploče, Pećine and Kostrena are pebble, fine pebble or concrete. The nearest beach with sand mixed into the shoreline is the city beach in Crikvenica, about 40 minutes by car.

faq.question: What is the nearest real sandy beach to Rijeka?
faq.answer: On Krk, about one hour by car, Sv. Marak near Risika and the beaches in Soline Bay are the closest true sand. Crikvenica is nearer, but its beach is a mix of sand and fine pebble.

faq.question: What is the best sandy beach for children near Rijeka?
faq.answer: Rajska plaža (Paradise Beach) in Lopar on Rab has about 1.5 km of fine sand and very shallow water. Crikvenica is the easier day trip from Rijeka, with shallow entry and facilities nearby.

faq.question: How do you get from Rijeka to Rab's sandy beaches?
faq.answer: Drive to Valbiska on Krk, then take the Jadrolinija ferry to Lopar, which takes about 80 minutes. Foot passengers can use the Jadrolinija catamaran linking Rijeka, Rab and Novalja.

faq.question: Which Rijeka beach is easiest to reach without a car?
faq.answer: Kantrida and Ploče are reached by city bus 1 from the centre. Bus 1 also serves the Pećine area. Both are pebble and concrete, so bring water shoes.

faq.question: Is Kostrena sandy?
faq.answer: No. Kostrena has fine pebble coves, and Žurkovo is pebble with some rocks. The water is clear, but sand is not part of it.

quickAnswer: Rijeka has no true sandy beach. Its beaches are pebble, fine pebble or concrete. The nearest sand-and-fine-pebble option is Crikvenica, about 40 minutes by car. Real sand is on Krk (about 1 hour) and Rab's Lopar peninsula (about 2.5–3 hours including the ferry from Valbiska).
